question: How tall is the Burj Khalifa in meters?

message.content: The Burj Khalifa is 828 meters tall. This height is consistently reported across multiple sources, including the official CTBUH (Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat) criteria and various references to its architectural height [5]. Some sources cite slightly different figures, such as 829.8 meters [1], 827.8 meters [4], or 829.8 meters to the tip [2], but the most widely recognized and official height is 828 meters.

passages.heading: Architecture and design
passages.text: The spire of Burj Khalifa is composed of more than 4,000 tonnes (4,400 short tons; 3,900 long tons) of structural steel. The central pinnacle pipe weighs 350 tonnes (390 short tons; 340 long tons) and has a height of 200 m (660 ft). The spire also houses communications equipment.<sup>[42]</sup> This 244-metre (801 ft) spire is widely considered vanity height, since very little of its space is usable. Without the spire, Burj Khalifa would be 585 metres (1,919 ft) tall. This was reported in a Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat study, which notes that the empty spire "could be a skyscraper on its own".<sup>[2]</sup> Such a skyscraper, if located in Europe, would be the 11th tallest building on that continent.<sup>[43]</sup>

passages.heading: Milestones
passages.text:
- 1 September 2008: Height tops 688 m (2,257 ft), making it the tallest human-made structure ever built, surpassing the previous record-holder, the Warsaw Radio Mast in Konstantynów, Poland.<sup>[110]</sup>
- 17 January 2009: Topped out at 829.8 m (2,722 ft).<sup>[111]</sup>
- 1 October 2009: Emaar announces that the exterior of the building is completed.<sup>[112]</sup>
- 4 January 2010: Burj Khalifa's official launch ceremony is held and Burj Khalifa is opened. Burj Dubai was renamed Burj Khalifa in honour of the President of the UAE and ruler of Abu Dhabi, Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed al Nahyan.<sup>[4]</sup>
- 10 March 2010: Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat certifies Burj Khalifa as world's tallest building.<sup>[113]</sup>

passages.heading: Awards
passages.text:
## Awards

In June 2010, Burj Khalifa was the recipient of the 2010 "Best Tall Building Middle East & Africa" award by the Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat.<sup>[158]</sup> On 28 September 2010 Burj Khalifa won the award for the best project of the year at the Middle East Architect Awards 2010.<sup>[159]</sup> Awards Chair Gordon Gill, of Adrian Smith + Gordon Gill Architecture, said:

We are talking about a building here that has changed the landscape of what is possible in architecture – a building that became internationally recognized as an icon long before it was even completed. 'Building of the Century' was thought a more apt title for it.<sup>[160]</sup>

passages.heading: Burj Al Khalifa: How Many Floors and Stories Does It Have?
passages.text: The Burj Khalifa’s highest floor accessible to the public is the 148th-floor observation deck at 555 meters. A second observation deck sits on the 124th floor at 452 meters. Above level 156, the structure transitions from concrete to steel, and the spire adds 242.6 meters to reach a total Burj Khalifa height in feet of 2,722 (829.8 meters to tip)—roughly three times the Eiffel Tower and nearly twice the Empire State Building.

passages.heading: Burj Khalifa View: Observation Decks and the Experience from the Top
passages.text: The experience of the tall Burj Khalifa is defined as much by movement as by form. The building contains 57 elevators, including double-deck units traveling at 10 meters per second, covering the longest elevator travel distance of any building at 504 meters. As cities grow vertically, architects must consider how such structures integrate into lived urban reality.

passages.heading: Burj Khalifa’s Legacy and the Future of Supertall Architecture
passages.text:
## Burj Khalifa’s Legacy and the Future of Supertall Architecture

The Burj Khalifa occupies a complex position in architectural history—simultaneously an engineering marvel, a cultural symbol, and a subject of critical debate. Its significance extends beyond record-breaking height, offering insights into how architecture operates at the intersection of technology, identity, and urban ambition. Notably, the Jeddah Tower in Saudi Arabia—designed by the same architect, Adrian Smith—aims to surpass it as the first building to exceed 1,000 meters.

passages.heading: List of tallest buildings
passages.text:
# List of tallest buildings

This is a list of the tallest buildings. Tall buildings, such as skyscrapers, are intended here as enclosed structures with continuously occupiable floors and a height of at least 350 metres (1,148 ft). Such definition excludes non-building structures, such as radio towers.

passages.heading: Height to roof
passages.text:
### Height to roof

This **list of tallest buildings by height to roof** ranks completed skyscrapers by height to roof which reach a height of 300 metres (984 ft) or more. Only buildings with continuously occupiable floors are included, thus non-building structures, including towers, are not included. Some assessments of the tallest building use 'height to roof' to determine tallest building, as 'architectural feature' is regarded as a subjective and an imprecise comparative measure. However, in November 2009, the CTBUH stopped using the roof height as the metric for tall buildings because modern tall buildings rarely have a part of the building that can categorically be deemed the roof.<sup>[115]</sup>

In April 2007, The Skyscraper Museum presented an exhibition on the skyscraper that was to become, and still is in 2020, the world's tallest building, Burj Khalifa. At the time called "Burj Dubai," the tower was under construction, on its way to 163 stories and ultimate height of 828 meters/ 2,717 ft. With the assistance of its architects and engineers at Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM), the Museum was able to present detailed material that documented and illustrated the design and construction of this structure of unprecedented height.

passages.heading: CONSTRUCTING THE BURJ SPIRE
passages.text:
### CONSTRUCTING THE BURJ SPIRE

It is one thing to draw a spire that reaches 828 meters into the air and to engineer the structure to support that height, but it is an added level of complication to figure out how it can be constructed.

passages.heading: SIGNIFICANT SKYLINES
passages.text:
Many cities, especially in Europe, restrict building heights. Our maps include five with significant skylines, but no buildings above 380 meters. Caracas and Johannesburg have the tallest skyscrapers on their continents. Toronto has nearly 1,700 high-rises and the 553-meter CN Tower, but its tallest skyscraper is only 298 meters. Singapore, with 3,763 high-rises, limits height to 280 meters and São Paulo with 4,541, has only one tower over 200 meters.

INSIDE THE ENGINEERING

How Burj Khalifa was built.

Design, structure and construction. Technical sources reviewed 9 September 2026.

SOM arranged three concrete wings around a six-sided core. Each wing braces the other two, while the central cell supplies torsional stiffness. The setback geometry aligns columns above with walls below, avoiding disruptive transfers as the floor plate reduces. Gravity and lateral resistance follow the same disciplined geometry.

A reinforced-concrete mat, 3.7 metres thick, distributes the tower load to bored piles 1.5 metres in diameter and 43 metres long. The mat was cast in four pours totalling 12,500 cubic metres. Low-permeability concrete forms part of the foundation durability strategy.

The Samsung C&T, Six Construct and Arabtec joint venture had to coordinate cranes, labour and material supply vertically. BESIX reports concrete pumping to 585 metres and cycles reaching two floors per week. Special mixes and predominantly night-time pours addressed temperatures exceeding 45°C.

Successive setbacks change the shape the wind encounters, reducing coherent vortex formation. The envelope uses silver-coated glazing to limit solar gain. Mechanical equipment is distributed through double-height service floors; the design also collects air-conditioning condensate for reuse. The steel spire was assembled inside the building and hydraulically raised into position.
